nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Co complex
nodes.procedure: tzbc (0.028 g, 0.15 mmol) and Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.095 g, 0.32 mmol) were dissolved in ethanol/water (4/2.5 ml) and stirred for 90 min. And then, above mixture was heated at 130 °C for 2 days. After natural cooling, precipitates were filtered and washed with ethanol to recover dark red block crystals.
nodes.source_text: For Co(tzbc)2(H2O)4 [32], tzbc (0.028 g, 0.15 mmol) and Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.095 g, 0.32 mmol) were dissolved in ethanol/water (4/2.5 ml) and stirred for 90 min. And then, above mixture was heated at 130 °C for 2 days.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Fe complex
nodes.procedure: tzbc (0.028 g) and Fe(NO3)2·9H2O (0.162 g, 0.40 mmol) were dissolved in ethanol/water (3/3 ml) and heated at 130 °C for 4 days.
nodes.source_text: Fe(tzbc)2(H2O)4 was obtained by adding 0.162 g (0.40 mmol) Fe(NO3)2·9H2O into in ethanol/water (3/3 ml) with 0.028 g tzbc and heating at 130 °C for 4 days

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni complex
nodes.procedure: tzbc (0.028 g) and Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.093 g, 0.32 mmol) were dissolved in ethanol/water (4/2.5 ml) and heated at 130 °C for 3 days.
nodes.source_text: Ni(tzbc)2(H2O)4 was obtained by adding 0.093 g (0.32 mmol) Ni(NO3)2·6H2O into in ethanol/water (4/2.5 ml) with 0.028 g tzbc and heating at 130 °C for 3 days.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal and nitridation of Co catalyst
nodes.procedure: 0.16 g graphene oxide (GO) was dispersed in 80 ml N,N-dimethylformamide and sonicated for 4 h to obtain a GO suspension. 0.1384 g Co(tzbc)2(H2O)4 was introduced into the GO suspension and subjected to magnetic stirring for 2 h. Subsequently, above mixture was subjected to hydrothermal reaction at 180 °C for 12 h. After drying, solid product was nitriding treatment at 800 °C with the feeding of Ar/NH3 (100/50 ml·min⁻¹). The nitridation process was carried out for 3 h to obtain Co@CoNx@NC-NG.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanoparticles of sizes 60 nm for Co@CoNx@NC-NG, 50 nm for Fe@FeNx@NC-NG, and 58 nm for Ni@NiNx@NC-NG with egg-like core-shell nanostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From high-magnification TEM images (Fig. 2d–f), the typical sizes of nanoparticles in Co@CoNx@NC-NG, Fe@FeNx@NC-NG and Ni@NiNx@NC-NG are about 60, 50 and 58 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show M@MNx@NC nanoparticles with uniform particle size homogenously encapsulated in NG support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Representative TEM and SEM images of M@MNx@NC-NG (M = Co, Fe, Ni) are displayed in Figs. 2a–c, S1, where M@MNx@NC nanoparticles with uniform particle size are homogenously encapsulated in the NG support.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns reveal only metallic Co, Fe, and Ni nanocrystals with no other metal-related crystalline species, confirming crystalline-amorphous core-shell structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Just as XRD spectra reveal that only metallic Co, Fe and Ni nanocrystals can be displayed in M@MNx@NC-NG (M = Co, Fe, Ni), and no other metal-related crystalline species (Fig. 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show ID/IG ratio of 1.1 for all M@MNx@NC-NG catalysts, indicating similar structural defects in carbon species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra show that the intensity ratio of D to G band (ID/IG) for M@MNx@NC-NG (M = Co, Fe, Ni) nanocomposites is 1.1 (Fig. 2h).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface areas are 505 m²/g for Co@CoNx@NC-NG, 489 m²/g for Fe@FeNx@NC-NG, and 475 m²/g for Ni@NiNx@NC-NG with dominant pore size at 4.0 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: BET areas of Co@CoNx@NC-NG, Fe@FeNx@NC-NG and Ni@NiNx@NC-NG, respectively, are 505, 489 and 475 m²·g⁻¹ (Fig. 2i), and the dominant pore size of M@MNx@NC-NG (M = Co, Fe, Ni) is centered at 4.0 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS shows metallic Co peaks at 777.90 eV and 796.50 eV, Co-N at 780.54 eV and 798.98 eV; N 1s shows pyridinic-N (398.08 eV), Co-N (399.19 eV), pyrrolic-N (400.42 eV), graphitic-N (401.73 eV); C 1s shows sp², sp³, C-N, C-O, O-C=O species. Similar metallic M, M-N, C-N bonds confirmed for Fe@FeNx@NC-NG and Ni@NiNx@NC-NG.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a shows the Co 2p XPS spectrum of Co@CoNx@NC-NG. The peaks at 777.90 and 796.50 eV are assigned to metallic Co [33, 34], which is in agreement with XRD result (Fig. 2g). The peaks at 780.54 and 798.98 eV can be ascribed to Co-N bond [33, 34]... the N 1s spectrum of Co@CoNx@NC-NG can be deconvoluted into pyridinic-N (398.08 eV), Co-N (399.19 eV), pyrrolic-N (400.42 eV) and graphitic-N (401.73 eV) [35] (Fig. 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS reveals uniform distribution of M (Co, Fe, Ni), C, N, and O elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results are consistent with the uniform distribution of M (M = Co, Fe, Ni), C, N and O revealed by energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Fig. S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows M@MNx@NC-NG catalysts have much lower charge transfer resistance compared to NG, indicating more efficient charge shuttle between electrode and electrolyte interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This can be confirmed by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technique (Fig. S13). Compared to NG, M@MNx@NC-NG (M = Co, Fe, Ni) composites exhibit much lower charge transfer resistance.
